issues.problem: R13-12 incomplete: the venv that make setup creates is invisible to make test and make coverage. run-all-tests.sh rebuilds PATH as a directory of symlinks, so tests run python3 through safe_bin/python3 -> .venv/bin/python3 -> /usr/bin/python3, and Python then does not detect the venv. Under make coverage the preflight passes (it runs in the parent with the venv python), but child processes cannot import coverage (the sitecustomize bootstrap swallows the ImportError), so Python coverage is not collected; openpyxl/PyYAML tests skip or fail. The Makefile's 'make test and make coverage use them automatically' message is false.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H3-probe/venvtest: python3 -m venv --without-pip .venv; module sbvenvprobe in its site-packages. 'PATH=.venv/bin:$PATH bash t/test-venv-probe.sh' -> 'venv package importable'. 'PATH=.venv/bin:$PATH bash tests/run-all-tests.sh t/test-venv-probe.sh' (from the worktree) -> 'venv package NOT importable', TOTAL 0 passed, 1 failed. Also: 'ln -s .venv/bin/python3 sb/python3; sb/python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.prefix!=sys.base_prefix)"' -> '/usr False'.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the Makefile export VIRTUAL_ENV=$(abspath $(VENV)) when the venv exists, and have run-all-tests.sh put "$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin" before safe_bin in TEST_PATH (or write 'exec "$_entry" "$@"' wrapper scripts instead of symlinks for python* found in a directory whose parent has pyvenv.cfg). run-all-tests.sh is outside H3's ownership: coordinate with its owner. Add a test that runs a probe test through run-all-tests.sh with a venv on PATH and asserts a venv-only module imports.

The release skills still run sync-release-marketplace-versions.sh before tagging and require that 'both upstream marketplace repos must have the same version committed and pushed', never run '--publish', and validate release notes after 'gh release create'. docs/RELEASE.md now says the skill 'walks through steps 6-9' and that notes are validated before publishing. A release driven by sb:create-release (the documented path) therefore never publishes the unified marketplace, and its stated gate condition is false.
issues.evidence: grep in the worktree: SKILL.md:213 'bash scripts/sync-release-marketplace-versions.sh "$VERSION"' under 'Step 5b.1' (before tagging); SKILL.md:220 'both upstream marketplace repos must have the same version committed and pushed'; SKILL.md:350 'validate-github-release-notes.sh --tag' after gh release create; no occurrence of '--publish' in skills/. The wrapper without --publish now prints 'Nothing was published'.
issues.suggested_fix: Update skills/silver-create-release/SKILL.md (add a post-tag Step 'sync-release-marketplace-versions.sh --publish', validate --file before gh release create, use --verify-tag) and skills/silver-release/SKILL.md:82, then run scripts/sync-codex-package.sh. Or, if the skill owner must do it, record it in files_changed_outside_ownership/notes as a required follow-up and land both together.

issues.problem: The workflow-hardening invariant accepts 'permissions: write-all', 'continue-on-error: ${{ true }}' or 'continue-on-error: "true"', and ${{ }} in actions/github-script 'script:' inputs. Nothing asserts that the CI checkout guard keeps --ignored, so the R13-05 fix can regress silently.
issues.evidence: Static reading: the permissions check is 'any(line.startswith("permissions:"))'; CONTINUE_ON_ERROR requires the literal true; only 'run:' blocks are scanned for ${{.
issues.suggested_fix: Reject write-all and any continue-on-error value, scan github-script 'script:' blocks, and add an assertion that ci.yml's guard uses 'status --porcelain --ignored'.

issues.problem: The full-history gitleaks scan on main, release-* and tags has never been run; history includes the worm commits and thousands of since-deleted files. If it flags anything, Secret Scan on main goes red and blocks verify-release-commit-ci.sh and --publish.
issues.evidence: gitleaks is not installed here (command -v gitleaks -> nothing); the author's validation simulates scan ranges only.
issues.suggested_fix: Run 'gitleaks detect --redact' over the full history once before merging and commit a .gitleaksignore/baseline for audited historical hits. Optionally pin the tarball's SHA-256 in the workflow, since a checksum from the same release only detects corruption.
